- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and prices are falling, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply 2–4% downward bias for first 7–10 days.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day window; if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 5–10% for next 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings (e.g., -0.33, 0.00, 0.20), model tends to ignore trend; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day average.
